126.question: The key purpose of a cultural code lies in...

options.A: Establishing a single language for all cultures
options.B: Eliminating the difference between a text and the object it denotes
options.C: Reducing a cultural message to the number of its symbols
options.D: Replacing any meaning with a physical property of the carrier
options.E: Linking a sign with its meaning and translating designations into senses

127.question: Different readings of a single cultural text when the code changes illustrate the proposition:

options.A: The code is identical to the author's intention in all cases
options.B: The meaning of a text is entirely determined by its length
options.C: The interpretation of meaning depends on the code applied
options.D: A text has no materially expressed signs
options.E: The difference between readings proves the absence of cultural meaning

128.question: Which statement about a cultural code is incorrect?

options.A: It helps to relate a cultural sign to its meaning
options.B: It influences the reading of one and the same cultural text
options.C: It changes only the material carrier while leaving the system of meanings unchanged
options.D: It helps to reveal the meaning of a ritual and a symbol
options.E: It can be transformed in the course of historical development

options.A: Biological heritability
options.B: Self-sufficiency
options.C: Fixed historical unambiguity
options.D: Openness
options.E: Universality

130.question: Why could a true name be hidden behind a commonly known one in ancient cultures?

options.A: The true name necessarily denoted the profession of its bearer
options.B: A name was considered inseparable from the thing and as allowing magical influence over it
options.C: Two names denoted an obligatory affiliation with two states
options.D: The commonly known name was used only in written laws
options.E: Sacred meaning was ascribed exclusively to a clan title

131.question: The example of the Christian reckoning of time from the coming of Christ shows that...

options.A: The cultural picture of the world is determined only by geography
options.B: Any code is reduced to the form of a written alphabet
options.C: A cultural code is limited to personal names
options.D: The organization of time can act as a code of the cultural picture of the world
options.E: Calendar time has no religious significance

132.question: Why can the concept of a code be considered broader than the concept of verbal language?

options.A: It describes only natural symptoms
options.B: It excludes the rules for organizing a message
options.C: It is not connected with the transmission of information
options.D: It is also applicable to non-verbal systems
options.E: It relates only to the sound composition of speech

133.question: In the concept of "code", Yu. Lotman emphasizes...

options.A: The fundamental absence of rules in artificial communication
options.B: The complete coincidence of a code with the centuries-long history of a natural language
options.C: Its association with an automatic model of communication, in contrast to a historical language
options.D: The obligatory polysemy of any machine message
options.E: The impossibility of applying the concept to technical languages

134.question: The special term "S-code" was proposed by...

options.A: J. Lacan
options.B: R. Jakobson
options.C: U. Eco
options.D: F. de Saussure
options.E: Yu. Lotman

135.question: The feature of reading connected with the S-code is...

options.A: Renouncing a definite point of view in interpretation
options.B: The dependence of the organization of understanding on a person's professional and other position
options.C: The independence of reading from education and experience
options.D: Reducing any message to a single literal meaning
options.E: The elimination of the rules of combinatorics from an utterance

136.question: The concept of the "subcode" for information systems with a hierarchy of codes is associated with the name of...

options.A: H.-G. Gadamer
options.B: A. Kroeber
options.C: E. Cassirer
options.D: C. Jung
options.E: R. Jakobson

137.question: The principle of the hierarchy of a cultural code means...

options.A: The obligatory superiority of written signs over oral ones
options.B: The equivalence of all interpretations in the absence of rules
options.C: The impossibility of combining several codes in a single system
options.D: A direct dependence of meaning on the length of an utterance
options.E: An ordered relation between a principal subcode and subordinate subcodes

138.question: What conclusion about the economy of message transmission did U. Eco propose?

options.A: Efficiency is determined only by the number of graphic signs
options.B: Any redundancy automatically destroys meaning
options.C: A limited number of combinations facilitates encoding and decoding
options.D: An unlimited growth of combinations always simplifies transmission
options.E: Economy requires a complete renunciation of rules of combination

139.question: Which psychological task is solved by a child's likening of himself to his parents in Freud's concept of identification?

options.A: Overcoming parental authority by means of rational criticism
options.B: Reducing fear by adopting the parents' power
options.C: Separating a conscious model of behaviour from the figure of a significant Other
options.D: Mastering a formalized language through a conscious agreement
options.E: Building an independent system of values before emotional identification

140.question: Emotional identification with a film hero initially leads primarily to...

options.A: The formation of a system of codes common to a society
options.B: The copying of the outward features of activity
options.C: An obligatory change of national affiliation
options.D: A complete loss of individual memory
options.E: Legal membership in a real organization

141.question: Assigning oneself to a nominal group is associated with...

options.A: The exclusion of emotional patterns of behaviour
options.B: The inheritance of the group's physiological features
options.C: A refusal to relate oneself to other people
options.D: Obtaining a formal identity document
options.E: The acquisition of socio-behavioural stereotypes

142.question: The distinguishing feature of identification with a real social group is...

options.A: The obligatory absence of shared values
options.B: A stable conviction of being involved in its norms and requirements
options.C: Only the short-term copying of a hero's appearance
options.D: Exclusively knowing the name of the group
options.E: Reducing belonging to genetic similarity

143.question: Reflexive acceptance of cultural evaluations is characterized by the fact that...

options.A: Evaluations are accepted only by the frequency of repetition
options.B: Evaluations are determined exclusively by the prestige of an idol
options.C: Evaluations are recognized as significant only when they fully coincide with everyone else's
options.D: Evaluations are borrowed without inner comparison
options.E: Evaluations are related to one's own experience before being accepted

144.question: As social development accelerates, the following characteristics of identities are strengthened:

options.A: Situationality
options.B: Mobility
options.C: The immutability of intergenerational models
options.D: Predetermination by a single inherited role
options.E: Lifelong fixation of group boundaries

145.question: As the diversity of cultural identifications increases, what persists is...

options.A: Complete dependence of identity on the place of birth
options.B: A single obligatory form of group belonging
options.C: The absence of subcultural differences
options.D: Identification as the realization of an existential need
options.E: An unchanging system of inherited social roles

146.question: Indicate the circumstances that can cause an identity crisis.

options.A: An age-related psychological crisis
options.B: A person's stable recognition by his group, in itself
options.C: A rapid change of the sociocultural environment
options.D: The preservation of intergenerational symbolic ties, in itself
options.E: The reconciliation of values with personal experience, in itself

147.question: Experiences associated with the loss of identity:

options.A: Reflexive rootedness
options.B: Depersonalization
options.C: Alienation
options.D: Stable involvement
options.E: Dialogical recognition

148.question: The ideal of authenticity differs from the fixed status identity of a traditional society...

options.A: By a call to discover one's own original way of being
options.B: By a demand to reproduce fully an inherited estate role
options.C: By reducing individuality to the father's profession
options.D: By eliminating the need for recognition by others
options.E: By a refusal of inner grounds of self-understanding

149.question: The condition for the recognition of different identities that Charles Taylor emphasizes is...

options.A: The absence of any common criteria of significance
options.B: A common moral background standing above individual ideals of authenticity
options.C: The elimination of all differences of cultural origin
options.D: The replacement of dialogue by administrative classification
options.E: A complete coincidence of the life experience of all groups

150.question: How does Z. Bauman distinguish the modern and the postmodern problems of identity?

options.A: To eliminate tradition; to renounce adaptation
options.B: To conceal one's origin; to restore an unchanging estate status
options.C: To create and preserve stability; to avoid fixation and keep the freedom of choice
options.D: To choose a profession; to acquire a genetic community
options.E: To renounce choice; to establish a single inherited role
